question: Let $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-1&-2\end{bmatrix}.$$ Determine all matrices $$B=\begin{bmatrix}p&q\\r&s\end{bmatrix}$$ for which $AB$ is the zero matrix, and hence exhibit a non-zero matrix $B$ satisfying $AB=O$ to establish the zero product behaviour of matrices.
explanation:
Formation of the Product

We have $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-1&-2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p&q\\r&s\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}p+2r&q+2s\\-p-2r&-q-2s\end{bmatrix}$$ For $AB=O$, every entry of this product must be zero. Therefore, $$p+2r=0,\quad q+2s=0$$ The remaining two equations are their negatives and give no additional conditions. Hence, $$p=-2r,\quad q=-2s$$ Therefore, every matrix of the form $$B=\begin{bmatrix}-2r&-2s\\r&s\end{bmatrix}$$ satisfies $AB=O$.

Construction of a Non-Zero Matrix

Choosing $r=1$ and $s=1$, we obtain $$B=\begin{bmatrix}-2&-2\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$$ which is clearly not the zero matrix. Direct multiplication gives $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\-1&-2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-2&-2\\1&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}=O$$ Thus, $A\ne O$ and $B\ne O$, yet $AB=O$. Hence, the product of two non-zero matrices can be the zero matrix.

options.D: $B=\begin{bmatrix}-2r&-2s\\r&s\end{bmatrix}$ for arbitrary $r,s$; for instance $r=s=1$ gives a non-zero $B$ with $AB=O$
